title: CLES-FACIL Rocket Design
text:
Preface
Welcome to the CLES-FACIL Rocket Design technical manual.
This repository serves as an interactive reference and tutorial guide for rocket design, created for members of the CLES-FACIL association (cles-facil.org).

title: CLES-FACIL Rocket Design
text:
About This Manual
Our goal is to provide clear, interactive, and highly visual explanations of complex rocketry concepts, inspired by modern interactive textbooks. Whether you are a beginner looking to understand the basics of aerodynamics, or an advanced member working on structural optimization, you will find useful resources here.

title: CLES-FACIL Rocket Design
text:
Contents
Currently, this manual covers:

Fin Design: Understand the impact of fin geometry on stability and aerodynamics through interactive sliders and visualizations.

More chapters on propulsion, recovery systems, and structures will be added soon.

title: CLES-FACIL Rocket Design
text:
Contributing
This manual is open-source. If you wish to contribute, please check our GitHub repository. We use Quarto for rendering these pages, allowing you to easily embed text, equations, and interactive Observable JS code blocks.

title: 1  Fin Design
text:
1.1 Interactive Fin Geometry
Adjust the parameters below to see how they affect the geometry and the aerodynamic properties of a standard trapezoidal fin used in model rocketry.
Code
viewof root_chord = Inputs.range([1, 20], {value: 10, step: 0.1, label: "Root Chord (Cr) [cm]"})
viewof tip_chord = Inputs.range([0, 20], {value: 5, step: 0.1, label: "Tip Chord (Ct) [cm]"})
viewof span = Inputs.range([1, 20], {value: 8, step: 0.1, label: "Span (S) [cm]"})
viewof sweep = Inputs.range([0, 20], {value: 4, step: 0.1, label: "Sweep Length (Xr) [cm]"})

title: 1  Fin Design
text:
1.2 Fin Characteristics
Based on the Barrowman equations for a single fin, the aerodynamic properties are calculated dynamically below:


Code
area = (root_chord + tip_chord) / 2 * span

// Center of Pressure distance from the root leading edge (simplified for trapezoidal fins)
Xf = (sweep / 3) * (root_chord + 2 * tip_chord) / (root_chord + tip_chord) + (1 / 6) * ((root_chord**2 + root_chord * tip_chord + tip_chord**2) / (root_chord + tip_chord))
















Calculated Results:

Fin Area:  cm²
Center of Pressure (Xf):  cm from the fin root leading edge

title: 1  Fin Design
text:
1.3 Fin Shape Visualization
Below is a generated 2D preview of the fin. The red dot represents the approximate geometric Center of Pressure for this single fin.


Code
Plot.plot({
  aspectRatio: 1,
  x: {label: "Length [cm]", domain: [0, Math.max(root_chord, tip_chord + sweep) + 2]},
  y: {label: "Span [cm]", domain: [0, span + 2]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(
      [
        {x: 0, y: 0},
        {x: sweep, y: span},
        {x: sweep + tip_chord, y: span},
        {x: root_chord, y: 0},
        {x: 0, y: 0} // Close the shape
      ], 
      {x: "x", y: "y", fill: "steelblue", fillOpacity: 0.5, stroke: "black", strokeWidth: 2}
    ),
    Plot.dot([{x: Xf, y: span/3}], {fill: "red", r: 5, title: "Center of Pressure"}),
    Plot.text([{x: Xf, y: span/3 - 1}], {text: d => "CP", fill: "red", fontWeight: "bold"})
  ]
})








1.3.1 Understanding the Parameters

Root Chord (Cr): The length of the fin where it attaches to the body tube.
Tip Chord (Ct): The length of the fin at its outermost edge.
Span (S): The radial distance from the root to the tip (how far it sticks out from the rocket body).
Sweep (Xr): The longitudinal distance the tip is set back from the root leading edge.

By tuning these parameters, we change both the aerodynamic drag and the position of the center of pressure. Shifting the Center of Pressure rearward generally increases the rocket’s static stability margin.
